To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
StackMap is a low-overhead, low-latency, and highthroughput Linux network service that can be used to build a new generation of network applications.

StackMap is an efficient, low-latency network service for the Linux OS stack that achieves comparable performance to a highly optimized user-level TCP/IP implementation, while retaining full compatibility with the standard socket API and the full-featured kernel TCP/IP stack.

StackMap achieves the best of both worlds, i.e., the performance of a kernel-bypass solution with a full-featured kernel stack, and it is the first solution to achieve this goal in a Linux environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to design, implement, and evaluate a low-latency, high-performance, and high-availability networking solution that can be used by applications running in a shared OS kernel environment.
the design and implementation of a new network service that can provide low-latency networking for Linux, while retaining its flexibility and full TCP stack.
the design and implementation of a novel, low-latency network service for the Linux operating system that can be used by any application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
StackMap offers a new, low-overhead, low-latency networking stack that is fully compatible with existing socket APIs.
StackMap provides the benefits of kernel-bypass while retaining the full-featured kernel stack.
the proposed StackMap is an excellent alternative to the existing user-level TCP stacks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can now offer a low-latency, high-throughput networking service for Linux that is as easy to use as the standard socket interface.
the OS stack is not the bottleneck in high-performance networking, and it is possible to build a high-performance networking stack that is based on the Linux kernel and socket API.
StackMap is a low-overhead, high-throughput, and latency-sensitive network service for Linux.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kernel-bypass is not the only way to improve networking latency and throughput.

it is possible to build a full-featured TCP stack that offers low latency and high throughput without sacrificing the flexibility of the socket API, by dedicating the network stack to the applications and offering an optimized data path.
it is feasible to achieve high-performance networking in a general-purpose Linux system with a full-featured TCP stack and the standard socket API, by dedicating NICs and using a zero-copy data path.
